Currently running Mint 19 and wanting to move to Debian Edition but not really cool with a clean install. Is there a tutorial somewhere on how to do an upgrade, so to speak, so that I can keep files and data that I have? I know, if it ain't broke don't fix it, but you know.

Thanks.
Is it possible to install Linux Mint Debian Edition without losing data in current Mint install?

It depends, did you install your /home directory to a separate partition? If so, then it's very easy to do. You just install the new operating system (LMDE) to the root (/) partition, designate your /home partition as the location of your files, and when it's complete, all your documents, settings, etc will remain in tact. Just reinstall the software you like (GIMP, LibreOffice, Hexchat, etc) and your settings will be just like before you changed operating systems.

If, on the other hand, you are using the same partition for your root and home directory, then it will take some more legwork. You will need to find a way to store your files onto a backup device, then transfer them back over after the install. The files you want to copy are everything under /home/username where 'username' is your actual username. When you install the new OS, make sure you set up your username to be identical to the one you currently use, and after installation is complete you just copy all of your files back into /home/username.

One of the nice things about Linux Mint is that there is a huge community, and many guides to help you get the first install method I mentioned. If you are going to upgrade, I highly, HIGHLY recommend finding a guide for dummies on setting up / (root) and /home on separate partitions. That way you can change distributions as often as you want, and not lose all of your documents and settings.

Hopefully this is helpful, or at least points you in the right direction to find the solutions you are looking for.
